name: Robotics and Engineering Design
title: Robotics and Engineering Design
answer: Robotics and engineering design give students real problems where a robot fails to turn or a bridge collapses, and they must work out why. AI can serve as a troubleshooting partner that asks what has been checked and suggests what to test next, while the student does the testing. This matters because the learning comes from failure, revision, and keeping the thinking with the student.

sections.body: This idea is about using AI to support hands-on robotics and engineering design without taking over the student's work. When something does not work, students face a genuine puzzle, and AI can prompt them to review what they have already tried and consider a next test. The problem it solves is that students can get stuck or discouraged, while a teacher cannot always be at every table. AI can help structure the design process and offer scaffolds at each stage, from defining the problem through building and improving. The scaffolds are meant to help students keep moving, not to tell them what to build.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or classroom, a teacher can use AI to draft scaffolds for the stages of engineering design: defining the problem, brainstorming, choosing a design, building, testing, and improving. These scaffolds support students who get stuck without giving them a finished design. Students can also use digital tools such as Tinkercad to design and test ideas before building them physically. The text does not give grade bands for this idea, so the same approach can be adapted to the age and materials at hand. Throughout, the student does the testing and the revising, which is where the learning happens.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text offers no study, figure, or evidence label for this idea. It presents the approach as resting on practice rather than research findings. The claim that a design which works on the first try teaches less than one that fails and gets fixed is stated as the book's position, not supported by a cited study. So this idea rests on practice rather than research.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: AI should never remove the struggle by handing students a design that is sure to work. The teacher's role is to keep the challenge real and to keep the thinking with the students. AI can ask questions and suggest tests, but the student must do the testing and the revising. The decisions about what to build, what to change, and when a design is good enough stay with the student and teacher. The limits are that AI is a troubleshooting partner and a scaffold builder, not a source of guaranteed answers.
